title: forgiving format autoformat
rule: Accept the value in whatever recognizable format the user types and autoformat it; do not force a single syntax.

citation.source: NN/g — A Checklist for Designing Mobile Input Fields; Designing Interfaces 3e ch. Getting Input — Forgiving Format (Tidwell, Brewer, Valencia)
NL Design System — Keur niet te snel af

pass_when: Recognizable variants are accepted and autoformatted.
fail_when: A single punctuation/syntax is required; other recognizable forms are rejected.
overview: Accept recognizable input formats and autoformat; do not force one syntax.
apply_when: Values users type in multiple recognizable formats (phone, date, etc.).
not_when: Strict identifiers that must match one exact syntax for integrity.
agent_hint: Accept recognizable variants and autoformat; reject only true unknowns.
description: Accept the value in whatever recognizable format the user types and autoformat it; do not force a single punctuation or syntax. Pass when recognizable variants are accepted and normalized; fail when one syntax is required and other recognizable forms are rejected. Forgiving format reduces false errors for phones, dates, and similar without inventing acceptance of unrecognizable junk the system cannot parse.
do_not_claim: HTML `pattern`/mask ban as this row; format-upfront copy as this row. Spectrum format-valid icon as this ban; placeholder as the format instruction (placeholder lock); `inputmode="numeric"` as a fail; don’t-reject-variants as this row.
